description: RTGS dollar launched as Zimbabwe's post-dollarization currency at an initial official rate of 2.50 per USD, ending the 2009-2019 multi-currency (mostly USD) regime.
Money supply roughly quadrupled over May-June 2023; ZWL depreciated approximately 83% on the parallel market (from ~Z$1070.42/USD to ~Z$6351.50/USD).
RBZ announced a new structured currency, ZiG, backed by gold and foreign-currency reserves, after ZWL had weakened past Z$30,000/USD.
ZiG formally replaced the ZWL at a conversion rate of 1 ZiG = 2498.7242 ZWL.
Zimbabwean dollar (2019-2024 series) formally decommissioned; ZiG stands as sole RBZ-issued local currency going forward.
Reserve Bank of Malawi devalued the kwacha by approximately 25% amid persistent forex shortages. Month-level precision only; exact day not confirmed in this research pass.
RBM devalued the kwacha by 44% and moved toward a more market-reflective rate, amid a severe dollar shortage, as part of IMF-backed reform discussions.
Shilling depreciated sharply through 2023 amid CBK/IMF-backed reforms to eliminate parallel FX rationing and move toward a more market-determined rate; reforms crystallized around Dec 2023.
